condition: Colorectal cancer — FIT-positive, non-specific abdominal pain
permutationLabel: FIT ≥ 10 is the only red flag
summary: 56-year-old woman with six weeks of vague lower abdominal discomfort, no bleeding, normal bowel habit and normal Hb; FIT 42 µg Hb/g. Under NICE DG56 the FIT alone mandates a suspected cancer referral.

inputs.hpi: Six weeks of vague lower abdominal discomfort, comes and goes, not related to meals. Bowels open daily, normal. No rectal bleeding, no weight loss. Post-menopausal, no vaginal bleeding. GP sent a FIT: 42 µg Hb/g.

exam.abdomen: Soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no mass.
exam.other: PR: normal, no mass, no blood.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: FIT-positive lower abdominal pain — colorectal cancer to be excluded
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Non-specific lower abdominal pain with FIT 42 µg Hb/g (≥ 10): suspected colorectal cancer pathway.

redFlags.note: The FIT result is the only red flag; the engines must read it.

guideline.name: NICE DG56 — quantitative FIT to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care
guideline.section: FIT ≥ 10 µg Hb/g → suspected cancer pathway referral
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Quantitative faecal immunochemical testing to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care (DG56). 2023.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI (updated 2023): refer adults with FIT ≥ 10 µg Hb/g
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

guideline.name: ACPGBI/BSG joint guideline — FIT in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer
guideline.section: FIT ≥ 10 µg Hb/g → urgent colonic investigation
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Davies MM, Abulafi M, et al. Faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) in patients with signs or symptoms of suspected colorectal cancer (CRC): a joint guideline from the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI) and the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG). Gut. 2022;71:1939–1962.

rationale: Permutation: every symptom-based red flag removed, FIT left positive. Isolates whether any engine reads a FIT result.

authoring.author: Claude (colorectal/anorectal cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Citations verified: false until checked against the source.
